dominant_strengths: Strong gallery curation with diverse type treatments — chunky display fonts, editorial serifs, and clean sans coexist credibly across tiles
Masonry grid handles varied aspect ratios well, creating rhythm without forcing uniform crops or flattening each site's identity
High craft visibility per-tile: each thumbnail reads as a complete composition with clear hierarchy, color story, and product hook
dominant_weaknesses: As an aggregate page the palette becomes noisy — saturated yellow, electric blue, orange, and dark teal compete without a unifying frame
Cookie banner and chrome feel tacked on; the persistent dialog covers a tile and breaks the immersive showcase intent
Minimal native Framer signature beyond hosting — the page itself doesn't demonstrate scroll/motion craft a 'scroll-500' brief implies
fix_priorities: Introduce subtle tile separators or muted backdrop to let saturated thumbnails breathe and reduce chromatic clash
Replace blocking cookie modal with a slim bottom bar so curation remains the hero
Add scroll-driven motion or hover micro-interactions to make the showcase itself feel Framer-native, not a static Pinterest grid
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral pull from vivid tiles is strong, behavioral scanability is solid via grid, but reflective payoff is muted because the meta-page adds little narrative beyond the sites it hosts.
rationale.intent_fit: Fits the 'scroll showcase of Framer sites' brief functionally, but underdelivers on demonstrating Framer's own motion and interaction capabilities.
